checkout has 0 server error spans out of 402 total spans — no own-work failures

Shipping p95 latency rose from ~40ms pre-onset to ~596ms post-onset (shifted=true), confirming a latency fault
Shipping is a leaf service with no registered callees; its latency is entirely internal or due to external HTTP calls it makes directly

Only shipping change is chg_4003 (runtime_config_change: 'shipping rate table updated for international zones', touching intl_rates and carrier_selection) at t=300, which postdates the t=250 onset

chg_4003 was ruled out as the cause of the initial onset (change at t=300 >= onset t=250), but it likely worsened shipping latency further — metrics_detect_shift found the largest shipping latency shift at t=1550, consistent with the config change taking full effect
Shipping is a latency victim/contributor but NOT the fault origin; the incident originated as a payment→unknown edge fault

feedback: The investigation went smoothly. The latency origin tool was immediately helpful pointing to shipping. The key challenge was that the alert onset (360) and the biggest latency shift (1550) didn't align - the degradation was intermittent before becoming sustained. The investigate_change subagent was very effective at confirming the config change matched the fault. The traces_span_tree on the slow trace was the definitive evidence showing shipping's ship-order as the bottleneck.
